In reality, nothing. Legally, the focus of one is on the sale of a product whereas the focus of the other is on recruiting.

The basic difference has to do with the way the people are compensated. A pyramid scheme puts no limits on the levels of people below you, whereas MLM requires limits in your downline.

 

Generally speaking, in a pyramid scheme, you take money from the new recruits, and use it to pay off what you owe the initial investors. It is illegal because the only way you can pay off initial investors is by getting more new recruits to supply the capital, but to pay off those new recruits, you need to get even more newer recruits, who then supply the needed capital to pay off the previous new recruits, and etc.... There will never people enough people to pay off everyone, hence, the last ones in are left holding an empty bag. Hence why it is illegal.

 

In MLM, you are basically a sales team trying to sell some product. When you sign up news sales guys, the products those guys sell will earn you a small %. There is a limit to how much that % can be before you no longer count as a MLM and now count as a pyramid scheme. Since MLM is just a sales job, there is really nothing wrong with it except for the fact that the products are usually overly expensive and most of the people you sign up are terrible at being salesmen (they often make false promises which can also be illegal). If you are not sure about a MLM, try buying the product for a while. If you think it is worth the money (it probably isn't), and you think you are great at selling stuff, then you could probably make some good money doing MLM on the side. But personally, I've never seen a MLM that sells a good product.
